skill.name: requesting-code-review
skill.description: Request structured code reviews after significant changes, before merges, or during plan execution to check requirements, tests, architecture, and readiness.
skill.summary: Guides teams to request structured code reviews before continuing development or merging changes.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: Most static warnings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder names, and example review text. I found no prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or malicious intent in the reviewed files. One medium concern remains because the review template embeds revision placeholders in executable git commands.

remediation.issue: Git diff commands use revision placeholders inside a shell block.
remediation.suggestion: State that BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA must be validated git revisions before execution, or show commands using already verified commit hashes only.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Git Revision Placeholders in Shell Commands
semantic_findings.description: The review template places {BASE_SHA} and {HEAD_SHA} directly inside git diff shell commands. If those values come from untrusted text instead of validated git revisions, a user who executes the block in a shell could run unintended commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are legitimate git review commands, but the placeholders are executable shell arguments. The risk depends on whether callers validate the revision values before use.

content.value_statement: Code changes can miss requirements, tests, or release risks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to request a structured review before merging.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to request review during feature work, plan execution, and merges.
Shows how to collect base and head git revisions for a review range.
Provides a reusable code-reviewer prompt template with required context fields.
Defines review categories for strengths, critical issues, important issues, and minor issues.
Instructs reviewers to give file-line references, reasoning, and merge readiness.
limitations: It does not run tests or inspect code by itself.
It depends on accurate task descriptions, requirements, and git revision inputs.
It cannot verify findings without repository access and reviewer execution.
It does not replace project-specific release gates or security review.

use_cases.title: Review completed feature work
use_cases.description: Request a structured review after finishing a major feature and before starting dependent tasks.

use_cases.title: Check plan execution batches
use_cases.description: Validate each batch of plan tasks against requirements, tests, and architecture expectations.

use_cases.title: Prepare a safer merge
use_cases.description: Ask for a final readiness review before merging changes into a shared branch.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after finishing a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my latest completed change against the task requirements. Identify critical, important, and minor issues before I continue.

prompt_templates.title: Pre-Merge Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the diff between the base and head revisions. Check correctness, tests, architecture, security, and merge readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Feature Completion Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after completing a feature from a written plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this completed feature against the implementation plan. Confirm fulfilled requirements, missing edge cases, and test gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Release-Critical Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for changes that affect production behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a production readiness review for this change set. Prioritize data loss, security, migration, compatibility, and rollback risks.

output_examples.input: A developer finished a verification feature and wants review before starting the next task.
output: Strengths: Clear structure, meaningful tests, and focused scope.
Important: Missing progress feedback could make long runs hard to monitor.
Assessment: Ready to continue after the important issue is addressed.

output_examples.input: A maintainer needs a final check before merging a multi-step implementation.
output: Strengths: Requirements are mostly covered and the architecture is consistent.
Critical: No blocking issue found during the review.
Assessment: Ready to merge with minor documentation follow-up.

best_practices: Request review after each meaningful task, not only at the final merge.
Provide the plan, implemented scope, base revision, and head revision together.
Fix critical and important findings before starting dependent work.
anti_patterns: Using the template without enough context for the reviewer.
Treating every concern as critical and losing prioritization.
Proceeding after valid important findings remain unresolved.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after major changes, after plan batches, or before merging.

faq.question: Does it perform the review automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives a workflow and prompt template for a reviewer agent.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can use prompt templates.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide what changed, the requirements, a base revision, a head revision, and a short description.

faq.question: Can it replace CI?
faq.answer: No. It complements tests, linters, and release checks.

faq.question: How should I handle disputed feedback?
faq.answer: Respond with technical evidence, tests, and clear reasoning before accepting or rejecting the finding.
